properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 5 at 2:17AM CDT until August 5 at 3:00AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
SVROAX

The National Weather Service in Omaha has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Montgomery County in southwestern Iowa...
Southern Mills County in southwestern Iowa...
Eastern Cass County in southeastern Nebraska...

* Until 300 AM CDT.

* At 217 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Pacific
Junction, or 12 miles southeast of Offutt AFB, moving east at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Glenwood around 220 AM CDT.
Malvern around 225 AM CDT.
Hastings around 235 AM CDT.

Other locations in the path of this severe thunderstorm include
Emerson.

This includes Interstate 29 between mile markers 27 and 32.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.
properties.area: Mills, IA; Montgomery, IA; Cass, NE

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 5 at 2:06AM CDT until August 5 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
FFWOAX

The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Mills County in southwestern Iowa...
Southwestern Pottawattamie County in southwestern Iowa...
Northeastern Sarpy County in east central Nebraska...

* Until 500 AM CDT.

* At 206 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bellevue and Offutt AFB.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
properties.area: Mills, IA; Pottawattamie, IA; Sarpy, NE

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 5 at 2:42AM EDT until August 5 at 5:45AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Berkeley County in southeastern South Carolina...
Charleston County in southeastern South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 238 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated brands of showers and a
few thunderstorms with torrential rainfall moving onshore across
much of eastern Berkeley County and upper Charleston County. Up
to and inch of rain has already fallen in some areas and an
additional 1 to 3 inches could fall through 530 AM, resulting in
minor flooding of low-lying and poor drainage areas.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mount Pleasant, McClellanville, Isle Of Palms, Sullivan's Island,
Awendaw, Jamestown, Garris Landing, Bull Island, Price Inlet and
Hampton Plantation State Park.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 4 at 11:53PM MDT until August 5 at 3:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Lower Seco Creek in Sierra County, New Mexico.

* WHEN...Until 300 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1153 PM MDT, Thunderstorms produced 1 to 1.5 inches of
rain over middle sections of Seco Creek tonight. While storms
have dissipated, runoff is likely to inundate the low water
crossing on Lower Seco Creek Road and Primaveras Road, just
under the I-25 underpass.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Lower Seco Creek near Caballo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
properties.sender: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 8:07PM CDT until August 6 at 8:10PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 32.0 feet, The Nueces River backs up minor creeks to
near the slab elevation of homes in the River Creek Acres
Subdivision, five miles southeast of George West. Livestock are cut
off and could drown in low areas of the flood plain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 33.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 9.0 feet Sunday evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 3:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 348 PM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing. Trees and debris larger
than telephone poles have been observed flowing down the
river. Between 1.0 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 7:51am the stage was 20.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest slightly above 22 feet late tonight and
into early Wednesday morning.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 8:45AM AKDT until August 5 at 5:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Petersville Area

* WHEN...Until 500 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 842 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Between 2 and 3 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to
1.5 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 11:03AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from good to moderate, but is forecasted to degrade.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM Wednesday, August 5, 2026.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
